item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q002_mazg_hise_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1vmga_ (MazG-like; a.204.1.2) and d1y6xa1 (HisE-like/PRA-PH; a.204.1.4) are distinct families within the same all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases superfamily, a.204.1 (and fold a.204). Their shared superfamily supports remote homology—a probable common evolutionary origin—rather than merely a similar fold, but it does not place them in the same close family. This evidence does not justify transferring the HisE phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphatase function to d1vmga_, assigning MazG activity to d1y6xa1, or inferring shared substrate specificity, catalytic mechanism, metal/ligand requirements, pathway role, or biological function. Such conclusions require independent biochemical evidence and, where relevant, detailed active-site and sequence/structure comparisons; superfamily membership alone is insufficient.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info — /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_/homology; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1/homology"]}]}
